title: Release Sprint Conductor: Cross‑Product Launch Harmony & Microtrain Schedule
creator: Maya Chen
description: Coordinate a repeatable small‑train (microtrain) cadence that harmonizes runtime, console, and API surface launches across teams. Deliver a lightweight conductor playbook, a templated weekly slot allocation, and capacity hedging guidelines so PMs/Eng/Design can self-serve scheduling without last-minute contention. Focus on predictable capacity reservations, preflight checks, and rollback criteria tailored to model-serving releases.
acceptance_criteria: Conductor playbook published in Confluence with step-by-step runbook
Weekly slot allocator template (spreadsheet + automation) available and adopted by 3 product teams
Capacity hedge policy codified (percent reserve, escalation path, fallback lanes)
Cutover decision tree and rollback thresholds agreed by runtime, infra, and SRE leads
Two dry-run rehearsals executed (one staging, one canary shadow) with documented learnings
milestones: 2025-02-14: Draft playbook and slot template (internal review)
2025-03-07: First microtrain slot allocation for Q2 sprint planning
risks: Overlapping capacity requests from large launches causing SLA degradation
Teams bypassing the conductor process and scheduling ad-hoc cutovers
Insufficient telemetry to detect model-regression impact during canaries
Automation cadence not matching org sprint rhythms (requires manual override)
notes: Proposal favors frequent small trains (1–3 teams) over monthly monoliths to reduce blast radius and speed iteration.
Key trade-off: tighter coordination adds calendar overhead; mitigated via templated automation and a single slot reserve steward.
Decision: adopt a 10% capacity hedge for microtrains during initial 6‑week ramp; revisit after telemetry stabilizes.
Follow-up: add slot allocator API endpoint to the Console by runtime-1.21 to automate capacity checks.
